q: A contract under which an agency both supplies the equipment and erects, tests and commissions it at site, as one composite responsibility, is in the nature of:

options.A: A pure labour contract
options.B: A zonal contract for petty repairs
options.C: A supply-cum-erection contract, in which the agency is responsible for the supply as well as for the erection and commissioning of the equipment
options.D: A contract for hiring of tools and plant only

e: A supply-cum-erection contract places single composite responsibility on the agency for supplying the equipment and also erecting, testing and commissioning it at site, unlike a pure labour, zonal or hiring contract under the GCC for Works.

q: The documents which together form a concluded works contract ordinarily include:

options.A: Only the formal agreement signed by the parties
options.B: The Letter of Acceptance, the General and Special Conditions of Contract, the specifications and drawings, and the priced schedule of quantities, read together with the formal agreement
options.C: Only the tender notice published in the newspapers
options.D: The completion report and the final bill of the work

e: A concluded works contract is read as a whole: the formal agreement together with the Letter of Acceptance, General and Special Conditions of Contract, specifications, drawings and the priced schedule of quantities, as provided in the Engineering Code and GCC.

q: During the execution of a work, the stipulated period of completion is extended on the contractor's request. The Performance Guarantee furnished by the contractor by way of a bank guarantee is due to expire before the extended completion date. The correct course is that:

options.A: The guarantee may be allowed to lapse, the work having been originally covered by it
options.B: The security deposit is forfeited automatically on the date of expiry of the guarantee
options.C: A fresh tender must be invited for the balance work in all such cases
options.D: The contractor is required to get the validity of the guarantee extended so that it remains in force for the extended period, including the defect liability period as applicable

e: Under the GCC, the Performance Guarantee must remain valid for the extended completion period including the defect liability period, so on extension of time the contractor must get the bank guarantee validity extended; it cannot be allowed to lapse.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tenders for the construction of a section of a new line should ordinarily be invited only when the land for the section is substantially available, so that the contractor is not held up for want of site.
2. Handing over of the site to the contractor is a matter unconnected with the progress of the work and the grant of extension of time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: tenders for a new line section are invited only when land is substantially available so the contractor is not held up for want of site. Statement 2 is wrong because timely handing over of site directly affects progress and extension of time.

q: A station yard remodelling work involves civil engineering works, signalling alterations and electrical installations, which must proceed in a co-ordinated sequence with the operating requirements of the yard. The co-ordination of the works of the different departments for such a work is ensured by:

options.A: Each department executing its portion independently at its own convenience
options.B: The contractor deciding the sequence of the departments' works on his own
options.C: Joint planning and periodical co-ordination among the departments concerned, so that each department's work is taken up and completed in the required sequence
options.D: Postponing all departmental works until the civil work is fully completed in every case

e: For interlinked civil, signalling and electrical works in a yard remodelling, the Engineering Code requires joint planning and periodical co-ordination among the departments concerned so each portion is done in the required sequence with operating needs.

q: In the course of executing a work, an existing underground water main and cables crossing the site have to be shifted before the foundation work can proceed. The shifting of such utilities is arranged by:

options.A: Ignoring the utilities and proceeding with the foundation work over them
options.B: The contractor demolishing the utilities at his discretion
options.C: Co-ordinating with the agency owning the utilities and getting them shifted or protected, the cost being dealt with as provided in the estimate and the contract
options.D: Stopping the work permanently, as utilities can never be shifted

e: Utilities crossing the site are shifted or protected in co-ordination with the owning agency before foundation work proceeds, and the cost is dealt with as provided in the estimate and contract; they cannot be demolished or built over at will.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before starting work, a contractor is ordinarily required to submit the organisation he proposes to deploy for the work, including the key technical personnel, in accordance with the contract.
2. Key personnel deployed on the work can be withdrawn or replaced by the contractor at any time without any reference to the Engineer.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: the contractor must submit his proposed organisation and key technical personnel as required by the contract. Statement 2 is wrong because key personnel cannot be withdrawn or replaced without reference to and approval of the Engineer.

q: For a major work, the contractor is required to set up a field laboratory at or near the site of the work primarily in order to:

options.A: Replace the departmental checks exercised by the Engineer
options.B: Store the contractor's tools and plant under lock and key
options.C: Serve as the site office of the Accounts department
options.D: Carry out the routine quality tests on materials and work, such as cube tests of concrete, at the site itself as the work proceeds

e: A field laboratory at site is required under the contract quality provisions to carry out routine tests on materials and work, such as concrete cube tests, as the work proceeds; it supplements and does not replace departmental checks.

q: Where the contract specifies that materials such as cement, steel or fittings shall be of particular approved makes, the contractor:

options.A: May use any make available in the market, the specification being only advisory
options.B: May charge extra for using the approved makes in all cases
options.C: Must obtain the materials only from the Railway's stores depot
options.D: Must use materials of the approved makes specified, and any equivalent make can be used only with the approval of the Engineer

e: Where approved makes are specified in the contract, the contractor must use materials of those makes only, and an equivalent make can be used only with the prior approval of the Engineer, as per the GCC specifications clause.

q: For critical operations under a contract, such as launching of girders or deep foundation work, the contractor is required, before taking up the operation, to:

options.A: Submit his method statement and scheme of execution for the approval of the Engineer, and carry out the operation in accordance with the approved scheme
options.B: Proceed entirely on his own judgement without informing the Engineer
options.C: Obtain the approval of the Tender Committee for the operation
options.D: Stop all other items of the work until the operation is over

e: For critical operations like girder launching or deep foundations, the GCC requires the contractor to submit a method statement and scheme of execution and obtain the approval of the Engineer before taking up the operation.

q: The design and adequacy of temporary works put up by a contractor for executing a work, such as staging, formwork and temporary supports, are:

options.A: The responsibility of the Railways, the contractor merely following the site practice
options.B: The responsibility of the contractor, who must ensure that they are safe and adequate for the work
options.C: Decided by the contractor's labour at the time of concreting
options.D: Certified by the Accounts office before use

e: Temporary works such as staging, formwork and temporary supports are designed and provided by the contractor, who remains responsible for their safety and adequacy under the GCC; the Railways do not take over that responsibility.

q: Instructions at the site of a work are conveyed to the contractor day-to-day by the representative of the Engineer posted at the site. Such a representative:

options.A: May alter the terms of the contract and sanction extra items on his own authority
options.B: Acts within the authority delegated to him by the Engineer, and instructions beyond that authority require the confirmation of the Engineer
options.C: Is competent to accept tenders for balance works at the site
options.D: Can release the security deposit of the contractor

e: The representative of the Engineer at site acts only within the authority delegated by the Engineer; instructions beyond that authority, such as altering contract terms or sanctioning extra items, require the confirmation of the Engineer.

q: A contractor is executing a station building work adjoining a platform in use by passengers. For the safety of the public and the workmen, the contractor is required to:

options.A: Carry on the work without any fencing, so that passengers can watch the work
options.B: Close the station to passengers for the entire period of the work
options.C: Provide proper barricading/fencing and, where necessary, lighting and warning arrangements around the work area, at his cost, as required by the contract
options.D: Pay compensation to passengers in lieu of providing any barricading

e: Under the GCC safety provisions, a contractor working near a platform in use must provide proper barricading or fencing and, where necessary, lighting and warning arrangements around the work area at his own cost for public and workmen safety.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. During a period for which the Engineer has ordered suspension of a work, the contractor is required to protect the work already executed and secure the materials at site.
2. Suspension of the work by the Engineer absolves the contractor of all responsibility for the work executed before the suspension.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: during suspension ordered by the Engineer, the contractor must protect the executed work and secure materials at site. Statement 2 is wrong because suspension does not absolve him of responsibility for work already executed.

q: During the execution of a work, the contractor is expected to keep the site of the work in a proper state, which includes that:

options.A: Surplus earth and debris may be dumped into the side drains and waterways of the track
options.B: Debris and waste materials are removed and disposed of at approved places, and drains and waterways are not obstructed by the work
options.C: Building materials may be stacked on the running track outside block hours
options.D: Excavated earth is the property of the contractor and may be sold by him in all cases

e: The contractor must keep the site clean and safe: debris and waste are removed to approved places and drains and waterways are not obstructed, as required by the GCC site management provisions; dumping in drains is prohibited.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. If a contractor fails to pay wages to the contract labour engaged on a railway work, the Railways, as principal employer, may become liable to pay the wages under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act.
2. Wages so paid by the Railways on behalf of the contractor can be recovered from the amounts due to the contractor.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, the Railways as principal employer may have to pay wages if the contractor defaults, and wages so paid are recoverable from amounts due to the contractor.

q: The insurance of a contractor's own tools, plant and equipment brought to the site of a work, against loss or damage, is:

options.A: Taken out and borne by the Railways as part of the departmental charges
options.B: The contractor's own responsibility, the works insurance under the contract covering the work itself and not automatically his own equipment
options.C: Waived in all works contracts as a matter of course
options.D: Covered by the earnest money deposited by the contractor

e: Insurance of the contractor own tools, plant and equipment is the contractor own responsibility; the works insurance under the GCC covers the work itself and does not automatically cover his own equipment.

q: Materials brought to the site by a contractor are lying at the site but have not yet been incorporated in the work. As regards payment for such materials in a running bill:

options.A: They are paid for at the full contract rates as if the work had been executed
options.B: Their cost is recovered from the contractor as a penalty
options.C: They are paid for at twice the schedule rate to encourage early procurement
options.D: No payment for the work is admissible on their account, payment being admissible only through a secured advance where the contract so provides

e: Materials merely brought to site earn no payment as work executed; payment on their account is admissible only as a secured advance where the contract so provides, under the GCC secured advance provisions.

q: Cubes cast from the concrete laid in a portion of a work give test results well below the specified strength. In such a case, the portion of the work represented by the failed cubes:

options.A: Must be paid for at the full rate, test results being only advisory
options.B: Is liable to be rejected, or accepted only after further investigation such as core tests and with such reduction or rectification as the Engineer directs under the contract
options.C: Is automatically treated as an extra item of work
options.D: Is certified by the Accounts office without reference to the Engineer

e: Work represented by concrete cubes failing the specified strength is liable to rejection, or acceptance only after further investigation like core tests with rectification or rate reduction as the Engineer directs under the contract.

q: A contractor's claim for extension of time and extra payment rests mainly on the plea that the Railways failed to hand over drawings and a part of the site in time. The record which will principally bear out or refute this plea is:

options.A: The comparative statement of the tenders for the work
options.B: The Hindrance Register maintained for the work, in which the hindrances and their periods were recorded and signed as they occurred
options.C: The contractor's ledger in the Accounts office
options.D: The abstract of the sanctioned estimate of the work

e: The Hindrance Register, in which hindrances and their periods are recorded and signed as they occur, is the principal contemporary record to prove or refute a claim based on late drawings or late handing over of site.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A settlement agreement arrived at through conciliation of a contractual dispute has, under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the status and effect of an arbitral award on agreed terms.
2. A settlement agreement through conciliation remains a mere proposal and can never bind the parties even after it is signed and authenticated.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 a settlement agreement through conciliation has the status and effect of an arbitral award on agreed terms. Statement 2 is therefore wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A contractor who wishes to pursue a claim under a contract must include the claim in the statement of claims/disputes submitted by him in accordance with the contract at the final settlement stage.
2. Claims which were never notified during the execution of the work, nor included in the contractor's statement of claims at final settlement, can be raised afresh at any time without limitation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: claims must be notified during execution and included in the contractor statement of claims at final settlement as per the GCC. Statement 2 is wrong because unnotified and unincluded claims cannot be raised afresh at any time.

q: At the completion of a work in which departmental materials were issued to the contractor and materials were also brought by him, a material reconciliation is prepared in order to:

options.A: Compare the materials actually consumed on the work with the theoretical requirement for the quantities of work executed, so that excess consumption or surplus materials are accounted for
options.B: Fix the rates for the next tender of the division
options.C: Decide the earnest money for future works of the contractor
options.D: Prepare the comparative statement of the tenders of the work

e: Material reconciliation compares materials actually consumed with the theoretical requirement for the quantities executed, so that excess consumption, shortages or surplus materials are accounted for at completion.

q: Before a completed asset is taken over, a joint inspection of the work is held and a list of the minor outstanding items and defects noticed is drawn up, which the contractor agrees to complete within a stipulated period. Such a list is commonly known as the:

options.A: Comparative statement
options.B: Liability statement of the division
options.C: Schedule of quantities
options.D: Snag list (punch list) of outstanding items

e: The list of minor outstanding items and defects drawn up at joint inspection before taking over, to be completed by the contractor in a stipulated period, is called the snag list or punch list.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Taking over of a completed work by the Railways does not, by itself, relieve the contractor of his obligation to rectify defects which appear during the defect liability period.
2. Once a work is taken over, defects appearing thereafter can never be got rectified by the contractor, even within the defect liability period.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: taking over does not relieve the contractor of his obligation to rectify defects appearing during the defect liability period. Statement 2 is wrong because such defects within that period must be got rectified by him.

q: An escalator installation executed under a works contract is being handed over by the construction organisation to the department which will operate and maintain it. The handing over of such an installation should be accompanied by:

options.A: Only the keys of the installation room
options.B: The tender documents of the contract alone
options.C: The contractor's final bill alone
options.D: The relevant test and commissioning certificates, operation and maintenance manuals and the guarantees/warranties of the equipment, along with the asset itself

e: Handing over of an installation must include the asset along with test and commissioning certificates, operation and maintenance manuals and equipment guarantees or warranties, so the maintaining department can operate it properly.

q: After the defect liability period of a completed asset has expired and the contractor's obligations are over, defects and repairs arising in the asset thereafter are attended to:

options.A: By the same contractor free of cost for the life of the asset
options.B: By recalling the original tender and re-awarding the work
options.C: Departmentally or through the maintenance/zonal contracts of the department maintaining the asset, as ordinary maintenance
options.D: Only after obtaining a fresh sanction of the Railway Board in each case

e: After the defect liability period expires and contractor obligations end, later defects and repairs are attended to departmentally or through maintenance or zonal contracts as ordinary maintenance, not by the original contractor free of cost.

q: A work required by a Zonal Railway is got executed through another Government agency, such as a public works organisation, on a deposit basis. In such an arrangement, the Railway:

options.A: Pays nothing, the agency bearing the cost as a grant
options.B: Recovers departmental charges from the executing agency
options.C: Deposits the estimated cost of the work, together with the agency/departmental charges of that organisation, with the executing agency
options.D: Treats the work as a deposit work received from an outside body

e: When a Railway work is executed by another Government agency on deposit basis, the Railway deposits the estimated cost of the work together with the agency or departmental charges of that organisation with the executing agency.

q: In a public-private partnership concession, the right of the lenders to step in and substitute the concessionaire with another entity, where the concessionaire defaults, is provided for primarily in order to:

options.A: Enable the lenders to take over the land of the project permanently
options.B: Transfer the authority's own obligations to the lenders
options.C: Terminate the concession automatically without notice
options.D: Protect the continuity of the project and the lenders' interests by substituting a capable operator in place of the defaulting concessionaire, with the approval of the authority

e: The lenders step-in and substitution right in a PPP concession protects project continuity and lenders interests by allowing a capable operator to replace a defaulting concessionaire with the approval of the authority.

q: In a toll-based concession, the concessionaire becomes entitled to commence collection of the user fee from the public ordinarily only after:

options.A: The Letter of Acceptance for the concession is issued
options.B: The project, or the relevant section of it, is completed and certified fit for use, that is, on reaching its commercial operation stage
options.C: The concessionaire has recovered fifty per cent of the project cost
options.D: The defect liability period of the works has expired

e: In a toll concession, user fee collection can commence ordinarily only after the project or relevant section is completed and certified fit for use, that is on reaching commercial operation, not on issue of the Letter of Acceptance.

q: The correct sequence in the finalisation of a works tender, after the tenders have been opened, is:

options.A: Opening of tenders, preparation of the comparative statement, examination and recommendations of the Tender Committee, acceptance by the competent authority and issue of the Letter of Acceptance
options.B: Issue of Letter of Acceptance, opening of tenders, preparation of comparative statement, recommendations of the Tender Committee
options.C: Recommendations of the Tender Committee, opening of tenders, issue of Letter of Acceptance, preparation of comparative statement
options.D: Acceptance by the competent authority, preparation of comparative statement, opening of tenders, recommendations of the Tender Committee

e: The correct tender finalisation sequence under the Engineering Code is: opening of tenders, comparative statement, examination and recommendations of the Tender Committee, acceptance by the competent authority, then issue of the Letter of Acceptance.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The List of Approved Works (LAW) lists the works sanctioned by the Railway Board.
2. Works sanctioned at the zonal level within the powers of the General Manager are listed in the zonal railway's own list of selected/sanctioned works programme, distinct from the Board's List of Approved Works.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Neither statement is correct as framed: the List of Approved Works is the programme list in the Pink Book compiled on prescribed cost criteria and is not confined to Board-sanctioned works alone, and GM-sanctioned works are not kept in a wholly separate list on that basis.

q: A number of similar small works are sanctioned together under one umbrella work. Before an individual work covered by the umbrella is actually taken up for execution:

options.A: No further estimate or sanction is needed for it, the umbrella sanction covering every individual work automatically in all respects
options.B: A separate open tender must be invited for the umbrella work as a whole once again
options.C: The individual work is executed straightaway against the Pink Book entry of the umbrella work
options.D: Its detailed estimate must be prepared and got sanctioned by the competent authority, and funds allotted, in the same manner as for any other work

e: Umbrella sanction does not dispense with individual sanction: before an individual work under an umbrella is taken up, its detailed estimate must be prepared and sanctioned by the competent authority and funds allotted, like any other work.

q: 'Test check' of measurements, as distinguished from 'check measurement', is:

options.A: A check of the measurements by the Accounts office at the time of passing the final bill only
options.B: A check exercised by the next higher engineering official over a proportion of the measurements recorded by a subordinate official, to satisfy himself of their general correctness
options.C: A fresh measurement of the whole work by an outside agency
options.D: A check of the rates quoted in a tender before its acceptance

e: Test check is the check by the next higher engineering official over a proportion of measurements recorded by a subordinate to satisfy himself of their general correctness, distinct from a full check measurement of the work.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Transactions between two Railways which are settled in cash by financial adjustment, instead of through transfer transactions in accounts, are known as IRFA transactions.
2. Transactions between two Railways which are settled through transfer transactions (book adjustment) in the accounts, instead of being settled in cash, are also known as IRFA transactions.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: inter-railway transactions settled in cash by financial adjustment instead of through transfer transactions are IRFA transactions. Statement 2 is wrong because book-adjusted transfer transactions are not IRFA transactions.

q: A division requires day-to-day housekeeping services for its stations, of a type commonly available as a standard service, while a major station building work is also to be arranged. The correct arrangement is that:

options.A: Both the housekeeping service and the building work must be arranged only through works tenders on IREPS
options.B: Both must be procured only through the Government e-Marketplace, works tenders not being permitted at all
options.C: The housekeeping service may be procured as a service, including through the Government e-Marketplace where applicable, while the building work is arranged through a works tender, including on IREPS
options.D: The housekeeping service must be executed departmentally and the building work procured through the Government e-Marketplace

e: Standard housekeeping services may be procured as services, including through GeM where applicable, while a building work must be arranged through a works tender, including on IREPS; the two follow their respective procurement routes.

q: Before the Notice Inviting Tender for a work is issued, the tender documents are vetted by Finance. A sponsoring officer treats this vetting as the Finance concurrence for the detailed estimate of the work itself. This understanding is:

options.A: Incorrect, vetting of the tender documents only settles the conditions to be included in them, while concurrence to the estimate is a separate examination of the proposal and its cost
options.B: Correct, vetting of the tender documents and concurrence to the estimate being one and the same act
options.C: Correct, because Finance concurrence is never required for a detailed estimate once a tender is to be invited
options.D: Incorrect only where the work is a deposit work

e: The understanding is incorrect: Finance vetting of tender documents only settles the conditions to be included in them, whereas concurrence to the detailed estimate is a separate examination of the proposal and its cost.

q: Administrative approval has been accorded to a proposed work on the basis of its abstract estimate, but its detailed estimate has not yet been sanctioned. In this position:

options.A: Expenditure can be incurred on the work straightaway, administrative approval by itself being the authority to spend
options.B: Tenders for the work can be accepted and the work started, only the completion report requiring sanction later
options.C: The contractor's running bills can be passed against the abstract estimate
options.D: Administrative approval only records approval in principle to the proposal; expenditure on the work can be incurred only after the detailed estimate is sanctioned by the competent authority and funds are allotted

e: Administrative approval is only approval in principle on the abstract estimate; expenditure can be incurred only after the detailed estimate is sanctioned by the competent authority and funds are allotted, as per the Engineering Code.

q: The expression 'risk and cost' in railway contracting is properly used for:

options.A: The purchase of stores from another source at the defaulting supplier's risk and cost
options.B: The completion of the balance work of a determined works contract through another agency at the cost and risk of the defaulting works contractor
options.C: The insurance of a work against all risks during its execution
options.D: The provision made in an estimate for contingencies and unforeseen items

e: Risk and cost in works contracting means getting the balance work of a determined contract completed through another agency at the cost and risk of the defaulting works contractor, under the GCC determination provisions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Assignment of a contract means that the contractor transfers his contract, or a benefit under it, to another party, which can be done only with the prior written consent of the Railways.
2. Novation of a contract means that a new contract is added alongside the original contract with a substituted party, the original contract continuing in force unchanged.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: assignment transfers the contract or a benefit under it and needs prior written consent of the Railways. Statement 2 is wrong because novation substitutes a new contract and party, extinguishing the original, not adding alongside it.

q: With the approval of the Engineer, a works contractor engages a sub-contractor for a specialised portion of the work. As between the Railways and the main contractor:

options.A: The main contractor is relieved of all responsibility for the portion sub-contracted
options.B: The sub-contractor becomes directly liable to the Railways in place of the main contractor
options.C: The main contractor remains fully responsible to the Railways for the whole work, including the portion executed through the sub-contractor
options.D: The Railways must settle the sub-contractor's bills directly

e: Sub-contracting with the approval of the Engineer does not relieve the main contractor, who remains fully responsible to the Railways for the whole work including the sub-contracted portion, under the GCC.

q: While evaluating a works tender, the Tender Committee examines the 'bid capacity' of the lowest tenderer, who is already executing several large works. This examination is directed at ascertaining whether:

options.A: The tenderer has quoted the lowest rate for every individual item of the work
options.B: The tenderer will have adequate capacity left, after meeting his commitments on the works already in hand, to execute the tendered work within the stipulated period
options.C: The tenderer's earnest money can be enhanced in proportion to his ongoing works
options.D: The tenderer is enlisted in the highest class of contractors of the Railway

e: Bid capacity assessment checks whether the tenderer, after meeting commitments on works already in hand, retains adequate capacity to execute the tendered work within the stipulated period, as per the tender evaluation criteria in the Works Manual.

q: Completion of a work is delayed partly by the Railways' failure to hand over a portion of the site and partly by the contractor's slow progress. Extension of time is under consideration. The correct approach is that:

options.A: The entire delay must be treated as the contractor's delay, the contract period being fixed once for all
options.B: The entire delay must be treated as the Railways' delay once any Railway failure is shown
options.C: Liquidated damages must be levied for the whole extended period in every such case
options.D: The period of delay attributable to the Railways and the period attributable to the contractor are assessed separately on the basis of the records, extension being granted without liquidated damages for the former and with liquidated damages, as applicable, for the latter

e: Delay is apportioned from the records: extension without liquidated damages for the period attributable to the Railways and with liquidated damages, as applicable, for the period attributable to the contractor, under the GCC extension provisions.

q: A contractor has been paid a secured advance against durable materials brought to the site for incorporation in a work. As the work progresses and the materials are consumed in the work:

options.A: The advance is recovered proportionately from the contractor's running bills, so that it is fully adjusted as the materials are incorporated in the work
options.B: The advance remains outstanding in full until the final bill of the work is settled
options.C: The advance is converted into a mobilisation advance of the contractor
options.D: The materials are returned to the contractor and the advance written off

e: A secured advance is recovered proportionately from running bills as the materials against which it was paid are incorporated in the work, so it is fully adjusted by completion, as provided in the GCC.

q: At the final settlement of a works contract, the contractor furnishes a 'No Claim Certificate' without any reservation and accepts the final bill in full settlement. The effect is that:

options.A: The contractor can raise fresh claims on the same contract at any time thereafter as a matter of right
options.B: The final payment is treated only as another on-account payment
options.C: The contract is treated as finally settled on the basis accepted by him, fresh claims on matters covered by the settlement not being ordinarily entertainable thereafter
options.D: The security deposit of the contractor becomes forfeited automatically

e: An unqualified No Claim Certificate with acceptance of the final bill in full settlement finally settles the contract on that basis, and fresh claims on matters covered by the settlement are not ordinarily entertainable thereafter.

q: A dispute under a works contract is first taken up for conciliation in accordance with the contract, but no settlement is reached and the conciliation fails. The dispute is then dealt with by:

options.A: Closing the dispute altogether, a failed conciliation barring all further remedy
options.B: Treating the conciliator's views as a binding award against both parties
options.C: Referring it back to the Tender Committee which dealt with the tender
options.D: Referring it to arbitration in accordance with the arbitration clause of the contract, at the instance of the party pursuing the claim

e: If conciliation under the contract fails without settlement, the dispute is referred to arbitration in accordance with the arbitration clause of the contract at the instance of the party pursuing the claim.

q: The distinction between a 'material modification' and a 'variation' in railway works is best brought out by the statement that:

options.A: A material modification relates to the sanctioned estimate and scope of the work and requires the sanction of the competent authority, whereas a variation relates to quantities or items within the execution of a contract and is dealt with under the conditions of that contract
options.B: A material modification relates only to the contractor's bills, whereas a variation relates only to the Pink Book
options.C: Both expressions mean exactly the same thing and are interchangeable
options.D: A variation requires the sanction of the Railway Board in every case, whereas a material modification is ordered by the contractor

e: A material modification concerns the sanctioned estimate and scope of the work and needs sanction of the competent authority, whereas a variation concerns quantities or items within contract execution and is dealt with under the contract conditions.

q: Expenditure is incurred on a work for which an estimate has been sanctioned, but no allotment of funds has been made for the work in the grant of the year. Such expenditure is objectionable as:

options.A: A deposit work executed without a deposit
options.B: Expenditure incurred without provision of funds, which forms a category of unsanctioned expenditure requiring regularisation
options.C: A work of urgent nature in all cases
options.D: A book adjustment requiring no regularisation at all

e: Expenditure on a sanctioned work without any allotment of funds is expenditure without provision of funds, a category of unsanctioned expenditure requiring regularisation, under the Engineering Code finance provisions.

q: On completion of a work, serviceable materials which had been issued for the work remain surplus with the contractor and are returned to the stores depot. In the accounts of the work:

options.A: The value of the returned materials continues to remain in the cost of the work
options.B: The returned materials are treated as the contractor's property and no adjustment is made
options.C: The value is credited to the earnings of the Railway as a sale receipt in all cases
options.D: The value of the serviceable materials returned is credited to the work, so that the cost of the work is reduced to that extent

e: Serviceable materials returned to stores are credited to the work, reducing its cost to that extent; their value does not remain in the cost of the work after return and accountal.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In an item-rate contract, the contractor is paid for the quantities of each item actually executed, at the rates quoted by him for those items.
2. In a percentage-rate contract, the contractor is paid at the schedule rates for the items, increased or decreased by the single percentage quoted by him.
3. In a lump-sum contract, the contractor is paid an agreed lump sum for the work as a whole, executed in accordance with the drawings and specifications.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 1 and 2 only
options.C: 2 and 3 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: All three are correct: item-rate pays measured quantities at quoted item rates, percentage-rate pays schedule rates varied by the single quoted percentage, and lump-sum pays the agreed lump sum for the work as a whole per drawings and specifications.

q: A work is well within the monetary powers of sanction of the General Manager, but it is of a type which figures in the list of matters excepted from the General Manager's powers (his negative powers). In such a case, the General Manager:

options.A: Can sanction the work, his monetary powers being sufficient for the purpose
options.B: Can sanction the work after obtaining the concurrence of the zonal Finance
options.C: Cannot sanction the work himself, the sanction of the higher authority prescribed for such matters being required despite the amount being within his monetary powers
options.D: Can sanction the work after recording the reasons in the Works Register

e: Even if the amount is within the General Manager monetary powers, a matter in the list excepted from his powers (negative list) cannot be sanctioned by him and requires sanction of the higher authority prescribed for such matters.

q:
Consider the following statements relating to a newly constructed railway line:
1. The line can be opened for the public carriage of passengers only after the sanction of the Commissioner of Railway Safety for its opening has been obtained.
2. On the opening of the line, the cost of the assets created is written off to Revenue and the completed work continues to be maintained by the construction organisation itself.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: a new line can be opened for public carriage of passengers only after sanction of the Commissioner of Railway Safety. Statement 2 is wrong because on opening the cost is transferred to capital-at-charge and maintenance passes to the open line organisation.

q: A post-completion evaluation of a major project, as distinguished from its completion report, is carried out primarily in order to:

options.A: Record the measurements of the work executed by the contractor
options.B: Compare the actual cost of the work with its sanctioned estimate for closing the estimate
options.C: Assess whether the project has achieved the objects and the financial results with which it was sanctioned, so that lessons are available for future appraisals
options.D: Settle the final bill and release the security deposit of the contractor

e: Post-completion evaluation assesses whether the project achieved the objects and financial results with which it was sanctioned, providing lessons for future appraisals; it is distinct from the completion report that closes cost against the estimate.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Block Account records each individual asset separately, with its location and the repairs carried out on it from year to year.
2. The Fixed Asset Register records the individual assets comprised in the capital-at-charge, asset-wise, with their cost and particulars.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 2 is correct: the Fixed Asset Register records individual assets in the capital-at-charge asset-wise with cost and particulars. Statement 1 is wrong because the Block Account is a summary by block or plan head, not an asset-wise record with repairs history.

q: On completion of a work, a report on the performance of the contractor is recorded by the executive. This record is principally of use when:

options.A: The rates for the contractor's next tender are to be fixed by the Railways
options.B: The contractor's enlistment is to be renewed, or his suitability for future works and tenders is to be considered
options.C: The completion report of the work is to be sanctioned
options.D: The departmental charges of the work are to be computed

e: The contractor performance report recorded on completion is principally used when his enlistment is to be renewed or his suitability for future works and tenders is considered.

q: The rate for an item of a proposed work is not available in the Unified Standard Schedule of Rates (USSOR). For framing the estimate of the work, the rate for that item is arrived at by:

options.A: Adopting the highest rate quoted in any tender received earlier for a different work
options.B: Omitting the item from the estimate altogether
options.C: Leaving the rate blank for settlement after the work is completed
options.D: Analysis of rates, worked out from the cost of the materials, labour and tools and plant required for the item, with the provision admissible for the contractor's overheads and profit where applicable

e: Where a USSOR rate is not available, the estimate rate is derived by analysis of rates from the cost of materials, labour and tools and plant required, with admissible provision for contractor overheads and profit where applicable.

q: At the closure of a work, the balance shown against the work in the Works Register is reconciled with the Contractor's Ledger and the related accounts mainly in order to ensure that:

options.A: The expenditure booked on the work, the payments made to the contractor and the recoveries and liabilities outstanding in respect of the work all agree, and nothing remains unadjusted
options.B: Fresh tenders for the balance work are invited without delay
options.C: The contractor is granted extension of time for the balance work
options.D: The estimate of the work is revised to match the lowest tender received

e: Closure reconciliation of the Works Register balance with the Contractor Ledger and related accounts ensures expenditure booked, payments made, and recoveries and liabilities outstanding for the work all agree with nothing left unadjusted.

q: The correct sequence for the execution of a deposit work on behalf of an outside body is:

options.A: Execution of the work, preparation of the estimate, deposit of the amount by the body, sanction of the completion report
options.B: Deposit of the amount by the body, preparation of the estimate, execution of the work, communication of the estimate to the body
options.C: Execution of the work, deposit of the amount by the body, preparation of the estimate, acceptance by the body
options.D: Preparation and communication of the estimate, acceptance by the body and deposit of the estimated amount including departmental charges, execution of the work, and adjustment or refund of the balance on completion

e: The deposit work sequence is: estimate prepared and communicated, acceptance by the body and deposit of the estimated amount including departmental charges, execution of the work, then adjustment or refund of the balance on completion, per the Engineering Code.

q: A works contract is foreclosed because the Railways no longer require the balance work, the contractor not being in default. In the settlement of such a foreclosed contract, the contractor is entitled, as provided in the contract, to payment for:

options.A: The full contract value, including the profit he would have earned on the work not executed
options.B: The work actually executed by him and the materials taken over from him, and not to the contract value of the work which was never executed
options.C: Nothing at all, the contract having been closed before its completion
options.D: Twice the value of the work actually executed by him, as compensation for foreclosure

e: On foreclosure without contractor default, the contractor is paid for work actually executed and materials taken over from him as provided in the contract, not for the contract value or profit on work never executed.

q: A contractor, against whom amounts are due to the Railways under a contract which has been determined for his default, is executing another work for the same Railway under a separate contract. The amounts so due may be dealt with by:

options.A: Writing them off, dues under one contract being incapable of adjustment against another contract
options.B: Recovering them only from the earnest money of fresh tenderers
options.C: Asking the Tender Committee of the other work to bear them
options.D: Recovering or setting them off against the amounts payable to the contractor under the other contract, in accordance with the contract conditions

e: Amounts due from a defaulting contractor under a determined contract can be recovered or set off against amounts payable to him under another contract with the same Railway, in accordance with the contract conditions.

q: Where a works tender is submitted by a joint venture and the tender conditions so provide, the earnest money and the performance guarantee for the work are ordinarily furnished:

options.A: Separately by every member for the whole amount, each member furnishing the full guarantee on his own
options.B: By the Railways themselves on behalf of the venture
options.C: Only by the member holding the smallest share in the venture
options.D: By the lead member on behalf of the joint venture, in accordance with the joint venture agreement and the tender conditions

e: In a joint venture, where the tender conditions so provide, earnest money and performance guarantee are ordinarily furnished by the lead member on behalf of the joint venture under the joint venture agreement and tender conditions.

q:
Consider the following statements in respect of a joint venture executing a railway work:
1. All correspondence and instructions of the Railways in connection with the work are channelled through the lead member authorised to act on behalf of the venture.
2. Despite this arrangement, the members of the venture remain jointly and severally liable to the Railways for the execution of the work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: all Railway correspondence and instructions are channelled through the authorised lead member, yet all members of the joint venture remain jointly and severally liable to the Railways for execution of the work.

q: In a two-packet tender, the technical bids are opened and evaluated first, and three tenderers are found technically acceptable. The financial bids to be opened and compared for deciding the lowest acceptable offer are:

options.A: The financial bids of all the tenderers who submitted bids, whether technically acceptable or not
options.B: Only the financial bids of the tenderers found technically acceptable, the remaining financial bids being returned unopened
options.C: Only the financial bid of the tenderer whose technical bid was opened first
options.D: None, the work being awarded on the technical bids alone

e: In a two-packet tender only the financial bids of tenderers found technically acceptable are opened and compared; the financial bids of the others are returned unopened, as per the tender procedure in the Works Manual.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A single tender may be justified where the requirement is of a proprietary nature obtainable from only one source, with the reasons recorded and the approval of the competent authority.
2. A single tender may equally be justified merely because the division is short of time in a routine case, without any recorded reasons.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: a single tender can be justified for a proprietary requirement from only one source with reasons recorded and competent approval. Statement 2 is wrong because mere shortage of time in a routine case without recorded reasons does not justify it.

q: Against a work in the Works Programme, only a token provision has been made in the budget for the year. The correct position regarding the taking up of that work is that:

options.A: The work can be commenced and executed in full against the token provision itself
options.B: The token provision authorises the acceptance of tenders for the whole work
options.C: The token provision merely keeps the work alive in the Programme; the work can be taken up only after its detailed estimate is sanctioned and adequate funds are allotted for it
options.D: The work is deemed to be sanctioned by the Railway Board by the token provision alone

e: A token provision only keeps the work alive in the Works Programme; the work can be taken up only after its detailed estimate is sanctioned and adequate funds are allotted for it.

q: A Railway sanctions a large number of new works every year while many earlier works remain incomplete for want of funds. The growing burden of the cost still to be incurred to complete all the works already sanctioned is known as the:

options.A: Throw-forward of the Works Programme
options.B: Material-at-Site balance of the Railway
options.C: Departmental charges of the works in progress
options.D: Liability under the contracts already awarded

e: The throw-forward of the Works Programme is the growing burden of cost still to be incurred to complete all works already sanctioned, when new works keep being added while earlier works remain incomplete for want of funds.

q: The proposals which a Zonal Railway submits for the Preliminary Works Programme are expected to be accompanied, for each proposed work, by:

options.A: Only the name of the contractor proposed to execute the work
options.B: The comparative statement of tenders for the work
options.C: The final bill of a similar work executed earlier
options.D: A justification of the need for the work, an indication of its cost and its financial implications, so that a selection of works can be made for the Programme

e: Preliminary Works Programme proposals must be accompanied by justification of need, an indication of cost and financial implications for each work, so a selection can be made for inclusion in the Programme.

q: Under a services contract for the cleaning of a station, the services rendered on a number of days are found to be deficient against the standards laid down in the contract. The deficiency is dealt with, in accordance with the contract, by:

options.A: Recording the measurements of the deficiency in the Measurement Book as a works item
options.B: Levying liquidated damages at the rate prescribed for works contracts in all cases
options.C: Effecting the proportionate deduction or penalty provided in the contract for the deficient service, after giving the contractor due notice as required
options.D: Determining the contract automatically without any notice for a single day's deficiency

e: Deficient services under a services contract are dealt with by the proportionate deduction or penalty provided in the contract for the deficient service, after due notice as required, not by works measurement or works liquidated damages.

q: An activity such as the cleaning of trains is got done through an outsourcing (services) contract. The supervision of the day-to-day work under such a contract is arranged so that:

options.A: The Railways directly supervise and discipline the individual workmen engaged by the contractor as their own staff
options.B: The contractor deploys and supervises his own staff, and the Railways supervise the output and quality of the service delivered under the contract
options.C: No supervision of any kind is exercised, payment being made on the contractor's claim alone
options.D: The Accounts office supervises the workmen at the site in place of the executive

e: In an outsourcing services contract the contractor deploys and supervises his own staff, and the Railways supervise the output and quality of the service delivered; Railway staff do not directly supervise or discipline the contractor workmen.

q: A pipeline of a public utility is to be taken across railway land, a commercial plot is to be given for long-term commercial use, and a small plot is to be allowed temporarily for a stall at a station. The three arrangements are respectively in the nature of:

options.A: Lease, licence and way-leave
options.B: Way-leave, lease and licence
options.C: Licence, way-leave and lease
options.D: Way-leave, licence and lease

e: A pipeline across railway land is a way-leave (permission to cross without interest in land), long-term commercial use of a plot is a lease, and a temporary stall at a station is a licence, as per the land management provisions of the Engineering Code.

q: A work for providing an additional loop and extending the existing loops in a congested section, so that more trains can be dealt with in the section, is in the nature of a:

options.A: Passenger amenity work
options.B: Staff welfare work
options.C: Deposit work
options.D: Line capacity work

e: Works for additional loops and extension of existing loops to handle more trains in a congested section are line capacity works, aimed at increasing throughput of the section.

q: For a proposed new railway line, the examination which is directed principally at assessing the traffic prospects of the line, its anticipated earnings and working expenses and, on that basis, its remunerativeness, is the:

options.A: Final Location Survey
options.B: Reconnaissance survey of the corridor
options.C: Techno-economic (traffic) survey of the proposal
options.D: Survey for the acquisition of land for the line

e: The techno-economic (traffic) survey assesses traffic prospects, anticipated earnings and working expenses of a proposed new line and, on that basis, its remunerativeness, as per the Engineering Code survey provisions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A work which is justified on safety considerations may be sanctioned even though it does not satisfy the normal test of financial remunerativeness applied to remunerative works.
2. Where such a work forms part of a larger scheme, the financial justification is examined only for the safety item in isolation, the rest of the scheme being ignored for this purpose.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: a safety-justified work may be sanctioned even if it fails the normal remunerativeness test. Statement 2 is wrong because where it forms part of a larger scheme, the financial justification of the scheme as a whole is examined.

q:
Consider the following statements relating to the close of a financial year:
1. The unspent balance of the allotment for a work lapses at the close of the financial year and is not carried forward automatically to the next year.
2. A rush of expenditure on works in the closing month of the year, merely to utilise the allotment before it lapses, is contrary to the canons of financial propriety.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: unspent allotment lapses at the close of the financial year and is not carried forward automatically, and a rush of expenditure in the closing month merely to utilise allotment violates the canons of financial propriety (GFR).

q: During the execution of a work, the Engineer gives an urgent oral instruction to the contractor at the site in an emergency. For the instruction to be acted upon and relied upon thereafter:

options.A: The oral instruction is sufficient by itself and needs no record of any kind
options.B: The instruction must be got confirmed in writing by the Engineer, oral instructions not so confirmed not being a proper basis for claims or for departure from the contract
options.C: The contractor must obtain the written confirmation from the Tender Committee
options.D: The instruction lapses unless the contractor himself records it in his own diary

e: An urgent oral instruction in an emergency must be confirmed in writing by the Engineer; an unconfirmed oral instruction is not a proper basis for claims or for departure from the contract, under the GCC.

q: A 'provisional sum' included in a detailed estimate of a work is an amount provided for:

options.A: The profit and overhead charges of the contractor who will execute the work
options.B: Work or items whose nature and extent cannot be fully defined at the estimate stage, the sum being expended as directed when that work is actually taken up
options.C: The departmental charges leviable on the work if it is executed for an outside body
options.D: The escalation in the prices of materials over the whole period of the work

e: A provisional sum in a detailed estimate covers work or items whose nature and extent cannot be fully defined at the estimate stage, and it is expended as directed when that work is actually taken up.

q: Under the approximate quantity method of preparing an approximate estimate of a building:

options.A: Every item of work is measured in full detail from the drawings and priced at schedule rates
options.B: The plinth area of the building is multiplied by the rate per unit of plinth area
options.C: Approximate quantities of the principal items of work are worked out from the preliminary drawings and priced at suitable rates to arrive at the rough cost
options.D: The length of the building is multiplied by a rate per running metre derived from other buildings

e: Under the approximate quantity method, approximate quantities of the principal items are worked out from preliminary drawings and priced at suitable rates to arrive at the rough cost of the building.

q: The 'plinth area' of a building means:

options.A: The built-up covered area of the building measured at the floor level of any storey
options.B: The area of the rooms of the building after deducting the area occupied by walls, verandahs and passages
options.C: The total area of the plot of land on which the building is constructed
options.D: The area of the roof of the building measured at its topmost level

e: Plinth area is the built-up covered area of a building measured at the floor level of any storey; usable area after deducting walls and passages is carpet area, not plinth area.

q: 'Cant excess' on a railway curve refers to:

options.A: The shortfall between the cant provided on the curve and the cant required for the equilibrium speed of trains
options.B: The cant provided on a straight length of track adjoining the curve
options.C: The easing of the gradient on the curve to offset the additional resistance of the curve
options.D: The excess of the cant actually provided on the curve over the cant required for the slower trains running over the curve

e: Cant excess is the excess of the cant actually provided on a curve over the cant required for the slower trains running over it; the corresponding shortfall for faster trains is cant deficiency.

q: A 'fouling mark' provided in a railway yard indicates:

options.A: The dead end of a siding at which a buffer stop is provided
options.B: The limit up to which vehicles may stand on a line without fouling, that is, obstructing, the adjacent converging line
options.C: The point from which the driver of an approaching train must sound the whistle
options.D: The point at which one track circuit ends and the next track circuit begins

e: A fouling mark indicates the limit up to which vehicles may stand on a line without fouling, that is obstructing, the adjacent converging line, as per the Permanent Way Manual.

q: Where an embankment for a railway work is to be formed on sloping or hilly ground, the ground under the filling is 'benched', which means that:

options.A: Pits are dug at approved places outside the formation from which earth is obtained for the embankment
options.B: A layer of blanketing material is spread over the formation before the ballast is laid
options.C: The sloping ground is cut into steps so that the new filling bonds properly with the slope and does not slide down over it
options.D: Stone pitching is provided on the slopes of the embankment to protect them from erosion

e: Benching means cutting sloping or hilly ground into steps under an embankment so the new filling bonds properly with the slope and does not slide over it.

q: 'Honeycombing' in concrete work refers to:

options.A: Voids and cavities left in the hardened concrete due to inadequate compaction or leakage of mortar, exposing the coarse aggregate
options.B: The appearance of water on the surface of freshly placed concrete after it has been compacted
options.C: The separation of the coarse aggregate from the mortar in fresh concrete during placing
options.D: The appearance of white deposits on the surface of the concrete due to soluble salts

e: Honeycombing is the voids and cavities left in hardened concrete due to inadequate compaction or leakage of mortar, exposing the coarse aggregate; it is distinct from bleeding, segregation and efflorescence.

q: 'Efflorescence' noticed on the masonry or plaster of a building is:

options.A: The voids left in the masonry due to inadequate filling of the joints with mortar
options.B: The rising of moisture from the ground into the wall above the plinth level
options.C: The separation of the plaster from the wall surface due to poor bonding
options.D: The white powdery deposit which appears on the surface due to soluble salts brought to the surface by moisture and left behind on its evaporation

e: Efflorescence is the white powdery deposit appearing on masonry or plaster due to soluble salts brought to the surface by moisture and left behind on evaporation.

q: The clear cover provided to the reinforcement steel in reinforced cement concrete work serves primarily to:

options.A: Increase the compressive strength of the concrete section
options.B: Protect the reinforcement against corrosion and fire and to ensure proper bond between the steel and the concrete
options.C: Reduce the deflection of the beam under load
options.D: Hold the stirrups of the beam in their correct position during concreting

e: Clear cover to reinforcement protects the steel against corrosion and fire and ensures proper bond between steel and concrete, as per RCC practice and the Works Manual.

q: A 'catch siding' provided in connection with a station on a steep gradient is a siding provided to:

options.A: Stable wagons in the yard for loading and unloading by merchants
options.B: Connect two parallel tracks so that trains can cross from one track to the other
options.C: Receive and arrest vehicles which may run away down the gradient towards the station, so that they do not foul the running line
options.D: Derail any vehicle which moves out of a siding without authority before it can reach the running line

e: A catch siding on a steep gradient receives and arrests vehicles that run away down the gradient towards the station so they do not foul the running line; derailing a vehicle leaving a siding is the function of a slip siding.

q: Cement brought to the site of a work by a contractor is required to be stored:

options.A: In a dry, weatherproof shed, stacked on a raised dry platform clear of the walls and the floor, and used broadly in the order in which it is received
options.B: In the open at the site, covered only with tarpaulins, as the normal method of storage
options.C: Along with the aggregates in the same stack so that both can be issued together
options.D: For an indefinite period, the order in which the consignments are used being immaterial

e: Cement must be stored in a dry weatherproof shed, stacked on a raised dry platform clear of walls and floor, and used broadly in the order received, as per the Works Manual storage provisions.

q: 'Pre-qualification' of bidders, as adopted for large and complex works, means that:

options.A: The eligibility of the bidders is examined only after their financial bids have been opened
options.B: The work is awarded to an enlisted contractor without inviting any bids
options.C: The enlistment of a contractor is renewed for a further period on the basis of his past performance
options.D: Intending bidders are first shortlisted on the basis of their experience, capacity and financial standing, and bids are invited only from those who are pre-qualified

e: Pre-qualification means intending bidders are first shortlisted on experience, capacity and financial standing, and bids are invited only from those pre-qualified, a method used for large and complex works under the GFR and Works Manual.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the two-packet system, the technical and financial bids are submitted together in two separate packets in a single stage, and the financial packets of the technically acceptable bidders alone are opened.
2. In two-stage bidding, proposals are invited and examined in the first stage and financial bids are called in the second stage from the shortlisted bidders.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: in the two-packet system technical and financial bids come together in separate packets in one stage and only technically acceptable financial packets are opened, while two-stage bidding examines proposals first and calls financial bids in the second stage.

q: While evaluating the tenders received for a work, the Tender Committee:

options.A: Must evaluate the tenders strictly in accordance with the criteria and procedure laid down in the tender documents, and cannot introduce any criterion not stated therein at the evaluation stage
options.B: May introduce additional criteria at the evaluation stage in order to obtain better value for the Railways
options.C: May relax the stated criteria in favour of the lowest tenderer after the tenders are opened
options.D: May substitute its own criteria for those stated in the tender documents with the approval of the Finance member alone

e: The Tender Committee must evaluate strictly per the criteria and procedure laid down in the tender documents and cannot introduce any new criterion at the evaluation stage, as per GFR transparency and fairness principles.

q: A deviation from the tender conditions noticed in a bid for a work is 'material' or 'minor' for deciding its responsiveness. The correct position is that:

options.A: Every deviation, however minor, makes the bid non-responsive in all cases
options.B: A tenderer may introduce a material deviation after the opening of tenders and still have his bid considered
options.C: Whether a deviation is material or minor is decided by the tenderer himself in his bid
options.D: A deviation which is minor and does not materially affect the scope, quality or price of the work may be waived while treating the bid as responsive, whereas a material deviation makes the bid non-responsive

e: A minor deviation not materially affecting scope, quality or price may be waived and the bid treated as responsive, whereas a material deviation makes the bid non-responsive, as per tender evaluation rules.

q: Under the Least Cost Selection method of selecting a consultant:

options.A: The technical and financial scores of the proposals are combined in the prescribed proportion and the assignment is awarded to the proposal with the highest combined score
options.B: The proposals which meet the minimum qualifying technical standard are compared, and the assignment is awarded to the lowest-cost proposal among them
options.C: The assignment is awarded to the lowest financial proposal without any technical evaluation at all
options.D: The consultant is selected on nomination, cost being settled by negotiation afterwards

e: Under Least Cost Selection, proposals meeting the minimum qualifying technical standard are compared and the assignment is awarded to the lowest-cost proposal among them, as per the GFR consultancy selection methods.

q: The enlistment (registration) of a contractor for railway works has the effect that:

options.A: The contractor becomes entitled to be awarded works in rotation in his section
options.B: Open tenders for works can be invited only from the contractors enlisted with the Railway
options.C: The contractor becomes eligible to be considered for works up to the limit of his class and for limited tenders, but enlistment by itself confers no right or assurance that any work will be awarded to him
options.D: The enlistment once granted remains valid permanently and is never reviewed

e: Enlistment makes a contractor eligible to be considered for works up to his class limit and for limited tenders, but by itself confers no right or assurance of award of any work.

q: A bidder who has been debarred under the General Financial Rules by a Ministry or Department of the Government:

options.A: Is ineligible to participate in the procurements of all Ministries and Departments during the period of debarment
options.B: Is ineligible only in the division which initiated the proposal for his debarment
options.C: Remains ineligible only for stores procurements and not for works contracts
options.D: Becomes ineligible only after the debarment is confirmed by a court of law

e: A bidder debarred under the GFR by any Ministry or Department is ineligible to participate in procurements of all Ministries and Departments during the period of debarment.

q: Before a works contractor can invoke the arbitration clause of the contract for a dispute, he is ordinarily required to:

options.A: Approach the civil court for appointment of an arbitrator in the first instance itself
options.B: Get the dispute examined afresh by the Tender Committee which dealt with the tender
options.C: Ensure that a conciliation of the dispute has first succeeded in his favour
options.D: First submit his claims to the Engineer for a decision in accordance with the contract, only the matters remaining in dispute thereafter being taken to arbitration

e: Before invoking arbitration, the contractor must first submit his claims to the Engineer for a decision in accordance with the contract, and only matters remaining in dispute thereafter go to arbitration, under the GCC dispute provisions.

q: In an EPC contract, the detailed design prepared by the contractor is got approved by the Authority's Engineer appointed for the project. The effect of such approval is that:

options.A: The responsibility for the correctness of the design passes entirely to the Railways on its approval
options.B: The approval does not relieve the contractor of his responsibility for the correctness and adequacy of the design prepared by him
options.C: The contractor is thereafter not required to follow the approved design during execution
options.D: The design becomes the responsibility of the Tender Committee which recommended the award

e: Approval of the contractor design by the Authority Engineer in an EPC contract does not relieve the contractor of responsibility for the correctness and adequacy of the design prepared by him.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For structural steel and similar fabrication work, the contractor prepares the detailed shop or fabrication drawings and gets them approved by the Engineer before taking up the fabrication.
2. Once the shop drawings are so approved, any error in them becomes the responsibility of the Railways alone.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: shop or fabrication drawings are prepared by the contractor and approved by the Engineer before fabrication. Statement 2 is wrong because such approval does not transfer responsibility for errors in them to the Railways alone.

q: The 'single-point responsibility' which characterises a design-build or EPC arrangement means that:

options.A: The contractor is responsible only for financing the project and not for its design
options.B: The Railways prepare the design and the contractor is responsible only for the execution of the work
options.C: The contractor bears the responsibility for both the design and the construction of the project, instead of the design resting with the Railways and only the execution with the contractor
options.D: The contractor operates the asset after construction and recovers his cost from the users of the facility

e: Single-point responsibility in design-build or EPC means the contractor bears responsibility for both design and construction of the project, instead of design resting with the Railways and only execution with the contractor.

q: Where new equipment or an installation is supplied, erected and commissioned by a contractor under a contract, the training of the staff who will work the asset is arranged as follows:

options.A: The Tender Committee imparts the training before the tender is accepted
options.B: The staff are in every case sent to the manufacturer's works abroad for training at the Railways' cost
options.C: No training obligation can be placed on the contractor under a works contract
options.D: Where the contract so provides, the contractor is required to impart training to the Railway staff nominated for operating and maintaining the equipment

e: Where the contract so provides, the contractor supplying, erecting and commissioning equipment must impart training to the Railway staff nominated for operating and maintaining that equipment.

q: Before an installation executed under a works contract is accepted and taken over by the Railways:

options.A: It is taken over on a visual inspection alone, tests being carried out after the defect liability period
options.B: It is subjected to the prescribed tests, trial runs and integrated commissioning checks, and is taken over only on its satisfactory performance in those tests
options.C: The tests are carried out only after the final bill of the contractor has been paid in full
options.D: The testing is entirely the contractor's internal matter, which the Railways cannot witness or verify

e: Before acceptance and taking over, an installation is subjected to prescribed tests, trial runs and integrated commissioning checks and is taken over only on satisfactory performance in those tests.

q: The periodical progress reports which a works contractor is required to submit during the execution of a work serve to:

options.A: Show the physical and financial progress achieved against the approved programme of execution, so that delays are identified and acted upon in time
options.B: Replace the measurements recorded in the Measurement Book for the purpose of payment
options.C: Record the attendance of the labour engaged by the contractor on the work
options.D: Compare the rates quoted by the contractor with the schedule of rates of the Railway

e: Periodical progress reports show physical and financial progress against the approved programme of execution, so delays are identified and acted upon in time; they do not replace Measurement Book records for payment.
